excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: Look, we love Notion conceptually but the SSO integration with Okta has broken three times in the last two months. Our IT team is spending 2-3 hours every time fixing it. At our scale that's real money. We need this to just work reliably before we can sign another year.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: The audit trail issue is a bigger problem for us. We're in financial services. Our compliance team did a review and Notion can't tell us clearly who edited what and when. That's a blocker for our regulatory requirements. If this isn't on the roadmap soon, we're going to have to look at Confluence for our sensitive content.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: I want to be clear — we like the product. Our teams are productive in it. But we have 230 users and two critical enterprise requirements that aren't being met. Fix the SSO reliability and give us a real audit log and we'll sign a multi-year deal. Without those, I can't justify the renewal to my CFO.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: We had a data loss incident. Our lead designer spent two days on a client presentation in Notion, and a simultaneous editing conflict wiped out about 30% of it. We had no backup. That killed trust for our whole team. Some people just refuse to use it now.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: I know you're telling me it's a known issue and the team is working on it. But we've heard that for eight months. Meanwhile my team is paying the price literally — we use Figma for design specs now and export to Notion manually, which is a massive workflow tax. This isn't sustainable.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: The pricing increase made things worse. We went from $15K to $18K this year and I had to fight for that budget. And then the data loss incident happened. My leadership is asking me why we're paying more for a product that lost client work. It's a really hard conversation.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: We want to expand Notion to our field teams — about 80 more people across 12 offices in different countries. But there are two blockers. First, our field teams need offline access. They're in areas with poor connectivity constantly. Second, the mobile experience is too slow for quick lookups. Our field reps would revolt.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: If you had offline mode, I could get you 80 more seats today. That's an easy decision. Right now I can't put those 80 people on a tool that requires internet to function. Even when they have connectivity, loading a page on mobile takes forever. The desktop is great but mobile has to be fixed.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: I've been a champion for Notion internally. I want this to work. But I need to be able to tell my VP of Operations that it will work reliably in the field. Can you give me any roadmap visibility on offline support? Even a rough timeline would help me make the case.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: The API performance is our main technical blocker right now. We built an internal product on top of the Notion API — about 1,200 rows in a database we query constantly. Response times are 3-7 seconds per call. Our engineers keep asking me if we should migrate to a real database. I keep defending Notion but it's getting harder.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: Search is the other one. We're three years in, we have thousands of docs. Finding things is genuinely hard. My suggestion would be full-text search across all content types, including inside table cells. Right now search just doesn't work for a company our size with our content volume.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: Our SOC2 auditor flagged the audit log as insufficient. They specifically called out that page moves, property changes, and bulk edits aren't fully attributed in the export. We have 90 days to remediate. If Notion doesn't have a path on this, we have to put a different tool in the audit scope, and that tool will probably also become our primary.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: The other concern is data residency. We have customers in the EU asking about where their information lives. Notion's answer of 'multi-region storage' isn't precise enough for procurement. Our competitors offer EU-only data residency. This is becoming a sales blocker for us, which weirdly puts pressure on our Notion contract.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: I'm telling you all this because we like Notion and we don't want to switch. But our renewal is in 60 days and we need at minimum a credible commitment on enterprise audit logging and data residency. Otherwise we have to start a procurement process for an alternative.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: I'm going to be direct with you — we're 95% sure we're leaving at renewal. The mobile experience killed it for us. Half my team is on the road for client meetings and they cannot function with the current iOS app. They've started using Apple Notes and emailing themselves things, which is exactly what Notion was supposed to fix.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: And the AI add-on. We turned it on, paid for a quarter, and the team unanimously asked us to turn it off. It can't see our actual content. So we're paying $10 a seat for ChatGPT with a Notion logo. Coda's AI literally answers 'what's our policy on X' from our actual handbook. That's the bar now.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: We have approval to expand by 200 seats across our warehouse and dispatch teams. But those teams have terrible connectivity in the field. Without offline mode this is a non-starter. Last quarter we even piloted with 30 of them and it was so frustrating they asked to go back to clipboards. Literal clipboards.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: The other expansion blocker is the API rate limits. We want to integrate Notion into our dispatch system as the workflow UI. The dispatcher updates a row, the system reacts. But at our throughput we'd hit rate limits in the first hour of every shift. Without an enterprise API tier we can't put Notion in any operational workflow.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: We're evaluating Notion against Confluence Enterprise. The user experience advantage is obvious — our team prefers Notion in trials. But our security team has hard requirements: SCIM v2 with deprovisioning hooks, customer-managed encryption keys, granular audit log with export, and field-level access controls. Where does Notion stand on those today?

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: Honest reaction: we hear 'on the roadmap' a lot. For a 600-seat purchase we need more concrete commitments. Our procurement requires SLAs in writing for SSO uptime and audit log completeness. Can you put us in touch with someone who can negotiate those terms?

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: We are your largest enterprise account in robotics. We have 1,400 seats. Our top three asks have been the same for 18 months: real-time collaboration without data loss, full-text search that actually works, and a workspace-aware AI. None of these have shipped meaningful improvements. I want to understand the prioritization.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: We had two data loss incidents in October alone. One affected our incident response runbooks. The fact that our IR runbooks could be silently lost during an editing conflict — I cannot keep them in Notion if that's the reality. We're piloting Confluence for runbooks just for this reason.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: I'll be candid: at my next board meeting I have to explain why we spend $320K a year on Notion. The answer needs to be more compelling than 'the team likes the UI'. I need to see roadmap commitments on the foundational issues, or we'll have to consolidate to a competitor.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: I've had a P1 ticket open for 12 days about our Salesforce sync breaking. We're getting a single email per day saying 'engineering is investigating'. Meanwhile our 35-person sales team has stale data in Notion and is making decisions on bad info. This level of support response for an enterprise integration is not acceptable.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: What I need from you today is one of three things: a real ETA, a workaround we can deploy this week, or a credit on next year's renewal. 'We'll keep you posted' is what I've gotten for 12 days. If this is what enterprise support looks like, I need to reconsider whether Notion is an enterprise-ready vendor.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: We left for Obsidian six months ago because of offline mode and search. I'm open to coming back if those are solved. But I need to see real evidence — not 'on the roadmap'. If you can show me Notion working offline on a plane today, I'll seriously consider it.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: The other thing that pushed us out was guest pricing. We're an architecture firm, we collaborate with 40+ contractors per project. Per-guest pricing made Notion 3x more expensive than alternatives for our use case. If you have an agency or project-based pricing model now, that would be relevant.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: Adoption has plateaued at about 60% of our staff. The remaining 40% report that the permission model is too confusing — they've accidentally shared things publicly twice this year. We've had to add a workspace-level rule that no one can toggle public sharing without IT approval. There should just be a workspace setting that disables public sharing.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: The other adoption killer is the search experience. Our teachers can't find lesson plans they wrote three months ago. We've started telling people to put a unique ID in every page title just to make search work. That's a workaround, not a tool.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: We're optimistic but we need to see search and permission improvements in the next two quarters or our IT director is going to make us pilot Confluence for the parts of the org where Notion isn't sticking.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: We have a 300-seat expansion plan parked. The blocker is compliance. Our auditor said the current Notion audit log can't satisfy our books-and-records retention requirements. We need event-level immutability and a tamper-evident export. Until that exists we cannot put advisor work product in Notion.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: Adjacent to that is data residency. Our regulator is asking where customer data lives. Notion's current answer doesn't pass our internal review. EU customers especially are pushing on this. If you had a true regional data residency story we could move on three deals waiting on us internally.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: Notion AI was the headline thing we expanded for. Six months in, our team has effectively stopped using it. The fundamental issue is it doesn't know our content. When our care coordinator asks 'what's our standard intake flow for new clients', Notion AI gives a generic answer. The actual intake flow is a page in our workspace.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: We're paying $9,600 a year for the AI add-on for 80 seats. If it's not workspace-aware in the next two quarters, we're cutting the add-on at renewal. We've evaluated Glean as an enterprise search and AI layer that sits on top of Notion. That's where the budget will go if Notion doesn't catch up.

excerpts.speaker: customer
excerpts.quote: The mobile and timeline view limitations are smaller things, but they add up. Our care managers in the field can't load patient notes quickly. Our project leads can't visualize program rollouts on a Gantt. Each of these on its own is fine, but together they make us evaluate alternatives every renewal.
